1003898.etyen:
From the initial letters of Aruba (A), Bonaire (B) and Curaçao (C) + øyene (“the islands”).
The final element, øyene (“the islands”), is the definite plural of øy (“island”), inherited from Old Norse ey (“island”), from Proto-Germanic *awjō (“island, floodplain”), from earlier *agwjō, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ékʷeh₂ (“water”).
Parallel formations include Papiamentu Islanan ABC, Dutch ABC-eilanden, Danish ABC-øerne, German ABC-Inseln, French îles ABC and English ABC Islands (“ABC Islands”).

Ved rikets oppløsning i 1806, falt kurverdigheten bort, bare Hessen-Kassel holdt på tittelen til 1866.
When the empire was dissolved in 1806, the electoral dignity ceased to exist; only Hesse-Kassel retained the title until 1866.

1004922.etyen:
From verdighet (“dignity, rank”), with the first element modelled after German Kur (“election”), as in kurfyrste (“prince-elector”). Compare German Kurwürde (“electoral dignity”).
German Kur is from Middle High German kür (“choice, election”), ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *kuʀi (“choice, decision”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵews- (“to test, taste, choose”). verdighet is verdig (“worthy, dignified”) + -het (“noun-forming suffix”).
Compare the parallel formations Danish kurværdighed, Swedish kurvärdighet and German Kurwürde (“electoral dignity”).
